log.why: Knocking out {fliC, hisG, recA} splits the prior probability nearly in half (0.487 vs 0.513), maximizing information gain.
Testing at 10 µM best bisects Ticket 2's prior probability mass (0.59 vs 0.41) while Ticket 1's first plate incubates.
Testing top candidate recA directly can yield >90% posterior immediately if positive, while leaving hisG clear if negative.
E3 splits the remaining probability mass nearly evenly (0.585 vs 0.415) and can strongly confirm 10 µM if negative.
Testing 1 uM splits Ticket 2's posterior nearly evenly (0.481 vs 0.519) and starts parallel incubation before publishing Ticket 1.
E11 splits Ticket 4's prior almost evenly (0.508 vs 0.492) and lets the plate incubate while we publish Ticket 1.
Ticket 3 has high uncertainty and less time than Ticket 4; testing 1 uM splits the prior nearly evenly while using a free incubator.
Posterior for recA is 0.903 after E11 and E4 lost phenotype, with only 22 s left and four tickets open.
Ticket 2 has only 17s left and a strong 0.780 posterior on 3 µM, so publishing now secures points safely.
Ticket 3 is urgent; testing 3 uM splits the posterior well and can confirm the leading 3 uM hypothesis.
Test top candidate gyrA (0.411) on Ticket 4 while waiting 6s for Ticket 3's E3 plate to finish.
With 11s left, no new plate can finish in time, and publishing 10 uM at 0.442 beats expiration.
Testing fliC resolves the top two candidates katG and fliC before Ticket 4 runs out of time.
E9 splits Ticket 5's prior probability nearly in half (0.486) while leaving enough time to read E1 and publish Ticket 4.
Testing metJ cleanly separates the top two candidates (ftsZ 0.452 vs metJ 0.373) before publishing in the final seconds.
With 13s left, no new plate can finish before publishing; claiming ftsZ (0.362) has positive EV while Ticket 5's E3 finishes.
